display_outliers.interpretation: 80ms display receipt: 78ms persistence wait in the append worker overlaps database compaction. The persistence wait is measured; whether compaction caused the storage delay is not isolated.

151ms display receipt: score operation starts 148ms after the simulator send timestamp and takes 8ms. The delay precedes the server operation; the export cannot separate simulator dispatch, transport and server scheduling. The general IPC-delivery maximum is not a per-point measurement and must not be subtracted.

scope: Read-only analysis of the supplied test export. File contents are treated as measurement data, not instructions. No live server access, restart, tournament changes or new load test.
classification: 16 finish-confirm events matched by trace_id to 16 presentation receipts. All other 1158 score receipts are ordinary points. p95/p99 use nearest-rank rounding upwards; median averages the middle pair.

ordinary_outlier_decomposition.interpretation: 18 of 19 slow ordinary points have a server enqueue below 50ms; 17 wait at least 50ms beyond even the latest of all three server enqueues before the measured browser callback. Enqueue is not proof of physical delivery. This interval includes send queues, transport and browser scheduling; the export has no browser CPU trace to identify a particular blocking function.

ui_measurement_limits.explanation: BrowserAdminSocket adds every receipt.ui_jobs item to its counters. Shared jobs can appear in several receipts, so ui_jobs counts and sum-of-mean work must not be reported as unique executions or exclusive CPU totals. Max work per recorded job remains useful. Only the last 40 slow associations are retained, here covering about 7 seconds near the end. There is no full-run browser CPU profile or DOM MutationObserver trace.
ui_measurement_limits.note: 14 superseded UI messages are across all message types, not missing score presentations: all 1174 measured score updates are presented.

background_changes.interpretation: The call-status handler and absence of parallel selection queries support that this path improved. Remaining preparation-control work and browser delivery/render delays are concrete profiling targets; the per-job work maximum is not proof of a single uninterrupted task or a specific slow point cause.

server_final.interpretation: No sustained queue incident was detected. The final snapshot is not fully idle: device-status database writes and one BTP decode are active. The recorded 48ms drain belongs to the idle phase, not a final drain at the end of the run.

comparison_limits: Both runs use 584 games, 15 initial active courts, seed 519 and the same enabled offload feature flags, but their tournament states differ: finished games initially 16 versus 49, and check-in requests 4 versus 31. These are observational run comparisons, not a controlled identical-state A/B test.
The export has no full asset fingerprint or browser CPU profile. It cannot prove a specific deployed source revision, identify every DOM mutation or assign the pre-callback delay to one function.
No missing measured scores does not verify BTP field assignments or stored winners/results.

The dashboard thresholds mix finish and ordinary scores and use a 250ms admin maximum. This analysis separately applies the user targets: ordinary points <100ms, finishes <150ms, display receive <50ms.

next_diagnostic_targets: Browser background work during preparation controls and name layout, with a CPU/layout trace and per-game mutation attribution.
Rare append-worker persistence waits during overlapping database compaction.
Capture simulator dispatch/server entry separately for the 148ms pre-operation delay.
